subject: BrightForge launch: temporary headroom / quota exception & traffic forecast
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sara Park <sara@brightforge.ai>
Date: 2028-04-18 08:22 -0700
Subject: BrightForge launch: temporary headroom / quota exception & traffic forecast

Team —

BrightForge (contact: Sara Park) confirmed an internal pilot becoming public on 2028-05-01. They expect a first-week spike and asked if we can provide a short-lived headroom bump to avoid throttles during onboarding. Quick context: BrightForge will run our chat endpoint for a product recommender; peak behavior is short-lived but very bursty (most requests arrive during campaign windows).

Key ask: can we provision a temporary quota/rate uplift for the week of 2028-04-30 to 2028-05-07 and route their requests to the dedicated burst pool to guarantee low tail latency? I attached their traffic forecast (brightforge_launch_forecast_v2.xlsx). Summary below:
- Expected baseline: 120 rps across US region (avg)
- Peak windows: ~850 rps for 6x 10-minute windows per day for 3 days during launch
- Total tokens/day estimate: 60M tokens (mixed gen / embed calls)

Questions for product/infra:
1) Sean — operationally, can we temporarily raise per-tenant qps and add a routing rule that pins them to dedicated burst nodes? What logs/metrics should we watch?
2) Irene — any model / config suggestions (smaller context windows or model variant) to keep latency while reducing cost?
3) Anyone — preferred approval/finance flow for the uplift and any pricing or credits we should offer?

Timeline: we need a decision + config by 2028-04-25 to schedule the routing change and a Canary on 2028-04-28.

Attachments: brightforge_launch_forecast_v2.xlsx (spreadsheet)

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Exec — Growth
Redwood Inference

From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sara Park <sara@brightforge.ai>
Date: 2028-04-18 09:05 -0700
Subject: Re: BrightForge launch: temporary headroom / quota exception & traffic forecast

Vanessa —

Thanks for the heads-up and the forecast. Quick read: peak shape is the main thing that matters. A few clarifying items before I sign off operationally:
- Are the 850 rps peaks sustained for 10 min continuously or are they microbursts within those windows?
- What percent of requests are streaming vs non-streaming? Streaming has different concurrent slot implications.

Operationally we can:
- Provision a temporary per-tenant QPS uplift (30min TTL) and an autotemp policy for the launch week; we will need the exact API key/tenant ID to pin.
- Create a routing rule to direct traffic to the dedicated burst pool; but that requires capacity reservations — I need PL/Finance approval for the extra headroom commit.

Monitoring: set up a dedicated dashboard (latency p50/p95/p99, error rate, token burn by route) and an alert if p99 > 600ms or error_rate > 0.5% during the peak windows.

Next steps from me: if you confirm the burst shape and provide the tenant ID, I’ll draft the Ops runbook and an infra change request (RFC).

—Sean
Site Reliability — Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: BrightForge launch: temporary headroom / quota exception & traffic forecast

Vanessa / Sean / Sara —

Thanks for the details. Product notes and constraints below. Short version: we can support the temporary uplift but have recommendations to reduce cost and tail risk.

Operational constraints:
- We cannot increase per-tenant qps beyond the cluster safety caps without a documented rollback plan and a readiness Canary.
- Routing to dedicated burst pool is possible if we reserve a small dedicated slab (recommendation: reserve enough for a steady 300 rps with burst headroom of 1k rps).

Recommendations:
- Model variant: run them on rwd-compat-2.1-small for public-facing sessions (cheaper, similar latency) and reserve rwd-compat-2.1-large for high-value sessions only.
- Implement token caps per request (e.g., max 512 tokens) during the first 72h to limit tail token burn.
- Use prefix/kV caching for repeat prompts (BrightForge has a lot of repeated product prompts).

Action items I need from BrightForge / Vanessa:
1) Tenant ID or API key prefix (so Sean can pin routing).
2) Confirmation that they accept the temporary token cap (512) for the first 72h.
3) A go/no-go by 2028-04-25 to start provisioning.

I’ll open an internal change request and attach the Canary playbook; linking the doc: https://redwood.docs/internal/launch-playbooks/brightforge-canary

Irene Choi
Director, Product — Serving
Redwood Inference

Perfect — thanks, noted. Quick confirmation and mutual action plan:

Mutual action plan (timeline):
- 2028-04-20: BrightForge to confirm tenant ID and acknowledge temporary token cap (Sara).
- 2028-04-21: Sean to provision reserved burst slab (300 rps steady, 1k rps burst) and create routing rule; Irene to open change request and Canary playbook.
- 2028-04-25: Finance/PL sign-off on temporary headroom commitment and any credits (Vanessa to coordinate).
- 2028-04-28: Internal Canary and smoke tests.
- 2028-05-01: Launch day; monitoring + on-call rotation: Sean (primary), Irene (product), Vanessa (AE escalation).

Sara — can you reply to this thread with the tenant ID and an explicit OK to the 512 token cap for the first 72 hours? If approvals are slow, please flag here and Vanessa will escalate.

I’ve attached a proposed quick patch with routing params (proposed_temp_quota_patch.txt) and the forecast. I’ll kick off the HubSpot task (https://app.hubspot.com/deals/1234567) for tracking and quote the temporary uplift in the renewal.

Thanks all — will follow up after Sara confirms.

Vanessa Ortiz
